```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Zecchin et al. (2026) describe how depemokimab, an ultra-long-acting anti-IL-5
monoclonal antibody, went from its first-time-in-human (FTiH) Phase I trial
straight to Phase III. Two blood eosinophil count (BEC) models carry the
argument, and both are packaged here:

1. `Zecchin_2026_depemokimab_dose_time` -- the Bayesian nonlinear mixed-effects
   dose-time response model fitted to the Phase I BEC data (Table 1). It is
   algebraic: BEC is a function of dose, time after a single dose and baseline
   BEC, with no PK. It selected the severe-asthma Phase III dose.
2. `Zecchin_2026_depemokimab` -- the mepolizumab population PK/PD meta-analysis
   model (an indirect-response model with inhibition of eosinophil
   production) re-estimated for depemokimab (Table 2). It selected the
   CRSwNP, EGPA and HES Phase III doses.

* Citation (dose-time model): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zecchin_2026_depemokimab_dose_time"))$reference`
* Citation (PK/PD model): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zecchin_2026_depemokimab"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70183>
* PK-layer source: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.70187>

# Population

The dose-time model was fitted to 622 BEC measurements from 48 adults with
mild-to-moderate asthma (BEC >= 200 cells/uL at screening, low-to-moderate
inhaled corticosteroid) who received a single subcutaneous depemokimab dose of
2, 10, 30, 100 or 300 mg or placebo in the FTiH trial (Study 205722). Only the
293 observations from Day 57 onward were used for estimation; the 47 Day 29
observations were held out for validation (Zecchin 2026 Results). Zecchin 2026
does not tabulate the cohort's demographics; the same 48 patients are
described in Thorsted 2026 Table 3: age 44.0 (SD 11.2) years, weight 82.9
(SD 11.6) kg, baseline BEC 366 (SD 147) cells/uL.

The PK/PD model's structure and all but four of its parameters come from the
mepolizumab population PK/PD meta-analysis (29,575 BEC measurements from 2516
participants in 16 studies, including 205 CRSwNP, 135 EGPA and 192 HES
patients). IC50, the two between-patient variances and the residual SD were
re-estimated on 675 BEC measurements from the same 48 FTiH patients.

# Source trace

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Dose-time model equation (active and placebo arms) | see model file | Zecchin 2026 Table 1, 'Model' row |
| E0, E1, E2, E3 | -0.2601, -0.6583, 0.5128, 0.5084 | Table 1 (posterior means) |
| Emax | -2.6047 | Table 1 |
| LNED50 (Day 182) | 2.9513 log mg (ED50 19.13 mg) | Table 1 |
| KE | 0.0207 /day (T1/2 33.5 days) | Table 1 |
| Hill slope (SLP) | 1.2358 | Table 1 |
| F (2 mg dose) | 2.3730 | Table 1 |
| Random-effect covariance (b1, b2, b3) | S2B rows | Table 1 |
| Residual variance (EPS, log scale) | 0.0804 (SD 0.2836) | Table 1 |
| Units of LNEOS / LNBASE | GI/L | Figure 1 y-axis |
| Indirect-response equation | `deos/dt = KOUT*(KRO*(1+(Imax-1)*C^GAMA/(C^GAMA+IC50^GAMA)) - eos)` | Zecchin 2026 Methods equation |
| KRO | exp(-1.73) = 0.177 GI/L | Table 2 (fixed, mepolizumab) |
| KOUT | 24*exp(-4.35) = 0.310 /day | Table 2 (fixed) |
| IC50 | exp(-2.34) = 0.0960 ug/mL | Table 2 (estimated) |
| Imax | exp(-1.77) = 0.170 | Table 2 (fixed) |
| GAMA | 1.61 | Table 2 (fixed); Supplementary Methods |
| BEOS1 on KRO, BEOS2 on Imax | 0.563, -0.380 (on log(BEOS/0.26)) | Table 2 (fixed) |
| SA, CRSwNP, EGPA, HES on KRO | 0.438, 0.132, 0.208, 1.27 | Table 2 (fixed) |
| Study 200622 multiplier on KRO | 0.5 | Table 2 (fixed) |
| BPV KRO, BPV Imax | 0.0853, 0.294 | Table 2 |
| Residual SD (log scale) | 0.350 | Table 2 |
| One-compartment PK, first-order absorption | structure | Zecchin 2026 Methods |
| CL/F, V/F, ka, Frel (FTiH asthma population) | 0.1063 L/day, 6.29 L, 0.345 /day, 0.827 | Thorsted 2026 Table S3 |

# Part 1 -- Bayesian dose-time response model

```{r mod1}
mod_dt <- readModelDb("Zecchin_2026_depemokimab_dose_time")
ui_dt <- rxode2::rxode(mod_dt)
ini_dt <- ui_dt$theta
```

## Derived quantities

Table 1 reports two derived quantities, ED50 = exp(LNED50) and the half-life
of the ED50 drift, log(2)/KE. Both follow from the packaged values.

```{r mod1-derived}
derived <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("ED50 at Day 182 (mg)", "T1/2 of the ED50 drift (days)"),
  Packaged = c(exp(ini_dt[["led50"]]), log(2) / ini_dt[["ked50"]]),
  Published = c(19.1308, 33.4854)
)
knitr::kable(derived, digits = 3, caption = "Derived quantities vs Zecchin 2026 Table 1.")
stopifnot(
  abs(derived$Packaged[1] / derived$Published[1] - 1) < 0.001,
  abs(derived$Packaged[2] / derived$Published[2] - 1) < 0.001
)
```

## Virtual cohort

Each arm of the FTiH trial is represented by 200 virtual patients (the trial
itself had about 8 per arm). Baseline BEC is log-normal with the Thorsted 2026
Table 3 mean (366 cells/uL) and SD (147 cells/uL) of the same 48 patients.

```{r mod1-cohort}
set.seed(20261)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261)
doses <- c(0, 2, 10, 30, 100, 300)
days <- c(28, 56, 84, 126, 168, 182, 224, 252, 280)
n_per_arm <- 200
sdlog_eos <- sqrt(log(1 + (147 / 366)^2))
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_per_arm * length(doses)),
  DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG = rep(doses, each = n_per_arm),
  EOS = exp(rnorm(n_per_arm * length(doses), log(366) - sdlog_eos^2 / 2, sdlog_eos))
)
ev_dt <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = days) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)
sim_dt <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_dt, ev_dt, keep = c("DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG", "EOS")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Replicate Figure 1

Figure 1 shows absolute BEC against dose for each scheduled day, with the
observed mean (black) and the model median (coloured). The black points below
were read from the published figure by the maintainers and are approximate.

```{r mod1-fig1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7}
fig1_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~dose, ~bec,
  28, 0, 0.35, 28, 2, 0.065, 28, 10, 0.065, 28, 30, 0.055, 28, 100, 0.065, 28, 300, 0.06,
  56, 0, 0.37, 56, 2, 0.065, 56, 10, 0.045, 56, 30, 0.042, 56, 100, 0.048, 56, 300, 0.06,
  84, 0, 0.36, 84, 2, 0.11, 84, 10, 0.055, 84, 30, 0.048, 84, 100, 0.058, 84, 300, 0.058,
  126, 0, 0.38, 126, 2, 0.16, 126, 10, 0.10, 126, 30, 0.062, 126, 100, 0.055, 126, 300, 0.06,
  168, 0, 0.37, 168, 2, 0.22, 168, 10, 0.19, 168, 30, 0.11, 168, 100, 0.05, 168, 300, 0.07,
  182, 0, 0.38, 182, 2, 0.25, 182, 10, 0.22, 182, 30, 0.12, 182, 100, 0.07, 182, 300, 0.06
)
sim_sum <- sim_dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(time, DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = median(blood_eosinophils),
    lo = quantile(blood_eosinophils, 0.025),
    hi = quantile(blood_eosinophils, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose_f = factor(DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG, levels = doses, labels = c("Placebo", doses[-1])))
fig1_obs$dose_f <- factor(fig1_obs$dose, levels = doses, labels = c("Placebo", doses[-1]))
ggplot(sim_sum, aes(dose_f, median, group = 1)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = fig1_obs, aes(dose_f, bec), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~time, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Dose (mg)", y = "Absolute BEC (GI/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Zecchin 2026: median and 95% interval of individual predictions; points read from the figure."
  )
```

The simulated medians track the observed dose-response at every day. The
placebo arm sits about 20% below the observed placebo means (0.30 vs about
0.37 GI/L), which with about 8 placebo patients is within the trial's own
scatter.

```{r mod1-fig1-check}
fig1_cmp <- fig1_obs |>
  dplyr::filter(dose > 0) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    sim_sum |> dplyr::select(time, dose = DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG, median),
    by = c("time", "dose")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(log_ratio = log(median / bec))
stopifnot(
  # Active arms, Days 28-182: the centre of the simulated medians matches the
  # observed means read from Figure 1 within about 25%.
  abs(median(fig1_cmp$log_ratio)) < log(1.25),
  quantile(abs(fig1_cmp$log_ratio), 0.9) < log(2)
)
```

## Dose for severe asthma (QDM pharmacology matching)

Zecchin 2026 compared the model's predicted Day 182 reduction from placebo
with the 78% (MUSCA, minimum value) and 84% (MENSA, target value) reductions
seen with mepolizumab 100 mg. The published go / no-go probabilities (Figure 2)
need the full MCMC posterior and the resampled trial ratios, which are not
available, so only the typical-value reduction is shown here. Because the
baseline slopes E2 and E3 are almost equal, the reduction is nearly
independent of baseline BEC.

```{r mod1-qdm}
qdm_doses <- c(10, 20, 30, 45, 60, 80, 100, 150, 200, 300)
ev_qdm <- data.frame(
  id = seq_along(c(0, qdm_doses)),
  DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG = c(0, qdm_doses),
  EOS = 366, time = 182, evid = 0, amt = 0
)
qdm <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_dt), ev_qdm, keep = "DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG") |>
  as.data.frame()
pbo <- qdm$blood_eosinophils[qdm$DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG == 0]
qdm_tab <- qdm |>
  dplyr::filter(DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reduction_pct = 100 * (1 - blood_eosinophils / pbo)) |>
  dplyr::select(DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG, reduction_pct)
qdm_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Single dose (mg)" = DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG, "Typical Day 182 reduction vs placebo (%)" = reduction_pct) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
red100 <- qdm_tab$reduction_pct[qdm_tab$DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG == 100]
red60 <- qdm_tab$reduction_pct[qdm_tab$DOSE_DEPEMOKIMAB_MG == 60]
stopifnot(red100 > 78, red100 < 84, abs(red60 - 78) < 3)
```

The typical reduction reaches the MUSCA minimum value of 78% at about 60 mg,
the dose above which Zecchin 2026 classified every regimen as "go", and the
chosen 100 mg dose gives about 81%, between the MUSCA and MENSA values.

# Part 2 -- PK/PD indirect-response model

```{r mod2}
mod_pd <- readModelDb("Zecchin_2026_depemokimab")
```

## PK layer and PKNCA check

Zecchin 2026 re-estimated a one-compartment, first-order-absorption PK model
on the FTiH data but does not print the estimates. The packaged model
therefore carries the published Thorsted 2026 depemokimab population PK model
(Table S3), evaluated for its "FTIH Asthma study population" and the Thorsted
reference covariates. Thorsted 2026 Table 2 reports the individual-predicted
exposure of the 9 FTiH patients for 100 mg every 26 weeks, which PKNCA can
check directly.

```{r mod2-pk}
regimens <- c(100, 200, 300)
pk_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 364, by = 1), 182 + seq(0, 21, by = 0.25))))
ev_pk <- lapply(seq_along(regimens), function(i) {
  rxode2::et(amt = regimens[[i]], ii = 182, addl = 1, cmt = "depot") |>
    rxode2::et(pk_grid) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = i, treatment = paste(regimens[[i]], "mg Q26W"))
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    EOS = 366, DIS_SEVERE_ASTHMA = 0, DIS_CHRONIC_RHINOSINUSITIS_NASAL_POLYPS = 0,
    DIS_EOSINOPHILIC_GRANULOMATOSIS_POLYANGIITIS = 0, DIS_HYPEREOSINOPHILIC_SYNDROME = 0,
    STUDY_200622 = 0
  )
sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pd), ev_pk, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

ggplot(dplyr::filter(sim_pk, time > 0), aes(time / 7, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "Depemokimab (ug/mL)", colour = NULL)

conc <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= 182) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
# The second dose (Day 182) is generated by addl inside rxode2, so it is not
# a row of the event table; give PKNCA the dose of the analysed interval.
dose_df <- data.frame(
  id = seq_along(regimens), treatment = paste(regimens, "mg Q26W"),
  time = 182, amt = regimens
)
o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 182, end = 364,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, clast.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))

published_pk <- data.frame(
  treatment = "100 mg Q26W",
  cmax = 12.29, tmax = 8.41, auclast = 778.8, clast.obs = 0.606, half.life = 39.4
)
knitr::kable(
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    simulated = nca, reference = published_pk, by = "treatment",
    units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", tmax = "day", auclast = "ug*day/mL", clast.obs = "ug/mL", half.life = "day")
  ),
  caption = paste(
    "Second dosing interval (Weeks 26-52), typical FTiH-population PK vs Thorsted 2026 Table 2",
    "(FTIH Asthma study, geometric means of individual predictions; Ctrough Week 52 compared with clast).",
    "* marks a difference above 20%."
  )
)
```

The typical values sit within about 10% of the FTiH geometric means. The
residual gap (typical clearance 0.106 L/day vs the FTiH individual geometric
mean 0.113 L/day) reflects the FTiH patients' weight (82.9 kg) and age (44
years) being away from the Thorsted reference subject (76 kg, 50 years),
which the packaged layer does not adjust for.

```{r mod2-pk-check}
nca_100 <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "100 mg Q26W", PPTESTCD %in% names(published_pk)[-1])
pk_cmp <- nca_100 |>
  dplyr::mutate(ref = unlist(published_pk[PPTESTCD]), pct = 100 * (PPORRES / ref - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(pk_cmp) == 5, all(abs(pk_cmp$pct) < 20))
```

## Replicate Figure 4

Figure 4 shows the predicted BEC at Week 52 after depemokimab 100, 200 or
300 mg every 26 weeks in CRSwNP (baseline 0.39 GI/L), EGPA (0.177 and
1 GI/L) and HES (1.46 GI/L). The typical-value predictions reproduce the
published geometric means only with two choices that the paper does not state
but that the figure pins down:

* **HES uses the Study 200622 multiplier** on KRO. GSK Study 200622 is the HES
  reference trial the panel is compared with. Without the multiplier the HES
  BEC is about twice the published value.
* **CRSwNP also carries the severe-asthma effect** on KRO (comorbid asthma).
  Without it the CRSwNP BEC is about 35% below the published value; with it
  the three CRSwNP points match to within 2%.

```{r mod2-fig4}
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~EOS, ~SA, ~CRS, ~EGPA, ~HES, ~ST,
  "CRSwNP, 0.39 GI/L", 390, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0,
  "EGPA, 0.177 GI/L", 177, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0,
  "EGPA, 1 GI/L", 1000, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0,
  "HES, 1.46 GI/L", 1460, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1
) |>
  tidyr::crossing(dose = regimens) |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = dplyr::row_number())

n_per_scen <- 200
ev_fig4 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  rxode2::et(amt = scen$dose[[i]], ii = 182, addl = 1, cmt = "depot") |>
    rxode2::et(c(0, 364)) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = i)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::left_join(scen, by = "scenario") |>
  dplyr::rename(
    DIS_SEVERE_ASTHMA = SA, DIS_CHRONIC_RHINOSINUSITIS_NASAL_POLYPS = CRS,
    DIS_EOSINOPHILIC_GRANULOMATOSIS_POLYANGIITIS = EGPA,
    DIS_HYPEREOSINOPHILIC_SYNDROME = HES, STUDY_200622 = ST
  )
ev_fig4_typ <- dplyr::mutate(ev_fig4, id = scenario)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pd), ev_fig4_typ, keep = c("panel", "dose")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 364) |>
  dplyr::select(panel, dose, typical = blood_eosinophils)

ev_fig4_sto <- lapply(seq_len(n_per_scen), function(k) {
  dplyr::mutate(ev_fig4, id = (scenario - 1) * n_per_scen + k)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20262)
sto <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pd, ev_fig4_sto, keep = c("panel", "dose")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 364) |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    geomean = exp(mean(log(blood_eosinophils))),
    lo = quantile(blood_eosinophils, 0.025),
    hi = quantile(blood_eosinophils, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Geometric means read from Zecchin 2026 Figure 4 by the maintainers.
fig4_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~dose, ~published,
  "CRSwNP, 0.39 GI/L", 100, 0.070, "CRSwNP, 0.39 GI/L", 200, 0.063, "CRSwNP, 0.39 GI/L", 300, 0.059,
  "EGPA, 0.177 GI/L", 100, 0.040, "EGPA, 0.177 GI/L", 200, 0.037, "EGPA, 0.177 GI/L", 300, 0.036,
  "EGPA, 1 GI/L", 100, 0.065, "EGPA, 1 GI/L", 200, 0.053, "EGPA, 1 GI/L", 300, 0.051,
  "HES, 1.46 GI/L", 100, 0.107, "HES, 1.46 GI/L", 200, 0.083, "HES, 1.46 GI/L", 300, 0.079
)
fig4 <- typ |>
  dplyr::left_join(sto, by = c("panel", "dose")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig4_pub, by = c("panel", "dose")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (typical / published - 1))

ggplot(fig4, aes(factor(dose), geomean, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = published), shape = 4, size = 3, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Depemokimab dose (mg Q26W)", y = "BEC at Week 52 (GI/L)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Zecchin 2026: simulated geometric mean (95% interval); x = published geometric mean."
  )

fig4 |>
  dplyr::select(panel, dose, typical, geomean, published, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = panel, "Dose (mg Q26W)" = dose, "Typical (GI/L)" = typical,
    "Simulated geometric mean (GI/L)" = geomean, "Figure 4 (GI/L)" = published,
    "Typical vs Figure 4 (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

stopifnot(
  # Typical values against the published geometric means; points read from
  # the figure carry about 5% reading error.
  abs(median(fig4$pct_diff)) < 5,
  max(abs(fig4$pct_diff)) < 10
)
```

The text of Zecchin 2026 gives the same results as reductions from baseline:
82% for CRSwNP at 100 mg, at least 79% for EGPA and 94% for HES at 200 mg.

```{r mod2-reduction}
red <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::mutate(base = c(0.39, 0.177, 1, 1.46)[match(panel, unique(scen$panel))]) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reduction_pct = 100 * (1 - typical / base)) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    (panel == "CRSwNP, 0.39 GI/L" & dose == 100) |
      (panel %in% c("EGPA, 0.177 GI/L", "HES, 1.46 GI/L") & dose == 200)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(published_pct = c(82, 79, 94))
red |>
  dplyr::select(panel, dose, reduction_pct, published_pct) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = panel, "Dose (mg Q26W)" = dose,
    "Simulated reduction from baseline (%)" = reduction_pct, "Published (%)" = published_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(red$reduction_pct - red$published_pct) < 2))
```

## Trough concentration relative to IC50

Zecchin 2026 states that 100 and 200 mg every 26 weeks give trough
concentrations about 5 and 10 times the IC50. The packaged PK layer gives
higher multiples:

```{r mod2-trough}
ic50 <- exp(rxode2::rxode(mod_pd)$theta[["lic50"]])
trough <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 364) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = Cc / ic50) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, Cc, ratio)
trough |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Week 52 trough (ug/mL)" = Cc, "Trough / IC50" = ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

The Week 52 trough after 100 mg (`r signif(trough$Cc[1], 3)` ug/mL) is close to
the Thorsted 2026 FTiH geometric mean (0.606 ug/mL), giving about 7 times the
IC50 rather than 5. The Zecchin 2026 PK estimates themselves are not
published, so the stated multiples cannot be checked directly; Figure 4, which
depends on the same concentrations through a steep part of the inhibition
curve, is reproduced to within a few percent.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PK layer from a different publication.** Zecchin 2026 does not report its
  depemokimab PK estimates. The packaged PK/PD model uses the Thorsted 2026
  depemokimab population PK model (same sponsor, fitted to the FTiH study plus
  two healthy-volunteer and four Phase III studies), evaluated for its "FTIH
  Asthma study population" (fractional effects on CL/F +15.5%, Frel -17.3%,
  ka +62.7%) at the reference covariates (76 kg, 50 years, non-Asian,
  albumin 45 g/L, eGFR 94 mL/min/1.73 m2, upper-arm injection). The body
  weight, age, albumin, eGFR, race, injection-site, 2 mg dose and PK IIV terms
  of Thorsted 2026 are not carried. The IC50 was estimated by Zecchin 2026
  jointly with their own PK, so the PK layer here is an approximation; it
  reproduces Figure 4 to within a few percent.
* **Fixed parameters.** Table 2 shades the mepolizumab-derived rows in grey;
  these (KRO, KOUT, Imax, GAMA and all covariate effects) are `fixed()`.
  IC50, the two between-patient variances and the residual SD are estimated.
* **Reference disease population.** The reference category of the KRO disease
  effects (all indicators 0) is not stated; it is the remaining meta-analysis
  population (healthy participants, mild-to-moderate asthma including the
  FTiH cohort, and eosinophilic oesophagitis).
* **Figure 4 scenarios.** The CRSwNP panel is reproduced with the
  severe-asthma indicator also switched on, and the HES panel with the Study
  200622 multiplier; see "Replicate Figure 4".
* **Point estimates of the Bayesian model.** The dose-time model uses the
  posterior means of Table 1, the column the paper's own derived quantities
  (ED50 = 19.13 mg, T1/2 = 33.5 days) are computed from. E3 has a skewed
  posterior (mean 0.5084, median 0.3425).
* **2 mg dose potency.** F is applied only when the dose equals 2 mg, as the
  Table 1 footnote states ("relative bioavailability of 2 mg dose").
* **Single dose only.** The dose-time model's time variable is days after a
  single dose; it does not describe repeated dosing.
* **Units.** LNEOS and LNBASE are on the GI/L (10^9 cells/L) scale, read from
  the Figure 1 axis; the covariate column `EOS` is in cells/uL and is divided
  by 1000 (dose-time model) or by 260 (BEOS/0.26 GI/L, PK/PD model).
* **Not reproduced.** Figure 2 (QDM probabilities) needs the MCMC posterior
  and the resampled MUSCA / MENSA ratios; Figure 3 (Phase IIb trial
  simulations) uses a separate negative-binomial exacerbation model whose
  parameters are not reported.
